title: 2013 HMMT February Geometry Problem 5
statement: In triangle \(A B C, \angle A=45^{\circ}\) and \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{B C}\). \(\overline{A M}\) intersects the circumcircle of \(A B C\) for the second time at \(D\), and \(A M=2 M D\). Find \(\cos \angle A O D\), where \(O\) is the circumcenter of \(A B C\).

solutions.text: \(-\frac{1}{8} \angle B A C=45^{\circ}\), so \(\angle B O C=90^{\circ}\). If the radius of the circumcircle is \(r, B C=\sqrt{2} r\), and \(B M=C M=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} r\). By power of a point, \(B M \cdot C M=A M \cdot D M\), so \(A M=r\) and \(D M=\frac{1}{2} r\), and \(A D=\frac{3}{2} r\). Using the law of cosines on triangle \(A O D\) gives \(\cos \angle A O D=-\frac{1}{8}\).
